items.followUp: What is meant by heat transfer?

rubric.why: Checks the definition of heat as energy transferred because of a temperature difference.
rubric.description: Defines heat as energy transferred from one body to another due to a temperature difference.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for both the energy-transfer idea and the temperature-difference cause; award 1 mark for either alone.

modelAnswer: Heat is energy transferred from one body to another because of a difference in temperature.

items.followUp: Convert 320 K into temperature on the Celsius scale.

rubric.why: Checks the conversion relation and the correct converted temperature.
rubric.description: Uses the Kelvin-to-Celsius relation and obtains the answer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the relation and 1 mark for the correct answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: T = 300 K
Formula: Temperature in °C = Temperature in K − 273
Substitution: T = 300 − 273
Answer: T = 27 °C

items.followUp: Derive the second equation of motion using a velocity-time graph.

rubric.why: Identifies the graph and obtains displacement as the area under it.
rubric.description: Uses the area under the velocity-time graph to write displacement as the area of a trapezium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the trapezium area and writing the displacement relation.

rubric.why: Uses the acceleration relation to express time in terms of velocity and acceleration.
rubric.description: Rearranges the acceleration equation to obtain an expression for time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either equivalent relation.

rubric.why: Checks the algebra and the correctly derived third equation of motion.
rubric.description: Substitutes the time expression and reaches the third equation of motion.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the correct derivation and final equation; award 1 mark for a valid substitution with an algebraic error.

modelAnswer: Draw a velocity-time graph with time on the horizontal axis, velocity on the vertical axis, and a straight line from velocity u at time 0 to velocity v at time t.
The displacement s is the area under the velocity-time graph.
Area of trapezium: s = 1/2 (u + v)t
Acceleration: a = (v − u)/t, so t = (v − u)/a
Substitute for t: s = 1/2 (u + v)(v − u)/a
Multiply by 2a: 2as = (u + v)(v − u)
Use the difference of squares: 2as = v² − u²
Therefore, v² = u² + 2as

items.followUp: Define kinetic energy and derive its formula.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of potential energy.
rubric.description: Defines potential energy as energy possessed by a body due to its position.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is energy due to position.

rubric.why: Checks the force and displacement used in lifting the body.
rubric.description: Identifies the lifting force as the body's weight and the upward displacement as h.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying weight mg and height h in the work calculation.

rubric.why: Checks the work calculation and the resulting potential-energy formula.
rubric.description: Uses work done against gravity to derive P.E. = mgh.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for a correct derivation and formula; award 1 mark if the correct formula is stated without a valid derivation.

modelAnswer: Potential energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its position.
When a body of mass m is lifted through a height h, the force applied equals its weight, F = mg.
Work done = force × displacement = mg × h = mgh.
This work is stored as potential energy; therefore, P.E. = mgh.

items.followUp: A force of 60 N acts on an area of 2 cm². Calculate the pressure in pascals.

rubric.why: Checks the stated data and conversion of area into SI units.
rubric.description: States the force and converts the contact area to square metres.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct data and area conversion.

rubric.description: Writes pressure as force divided by area.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

rubric.why: Checks substitution, calculation, and the final SI unit.
rubric.description: Substitutes the SI values and calculates the pressure.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution, 1 mark for the correct numerical result, and 1 mark for the correct unit.

modelAnswer: Given: Force, F = 75 N
Given: Contact area, A = 1.5 cm² = 1.5 × 10⁻⁴ m²
Formula: Pressure, P = F/A
Substitution: P = 75 N/(1.5 × 10⁻⁴ m²)
Answer: P = 5 × 10⁵ Pa

items.followUp: Differentiate between a base quantity and a derived quantity, giving one example of each.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of base units.
rubric.description: States that base units are independent units not defined in terms of other units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct distinction.

rubric.why: Checks how derived units are formed.
rubric.description: States that derived units are formed by combining base units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct distinction.

modelAnswer: Base units are independent units that are not derived from other units; for example, the metre (m).
Derived units are obtained by combining base units; for example, the metre per second (m/s).

items.followUp: What is the least count of a measuring tape marked in millimetres?

rubric.why: Checks the definition of least count.
rubric.description: Defines least count as the smallest measurement that an instrument can measure accurately.

rubric.why: Checks the least count of a metre rule.
rubric.description: Gives the least count of a metre rule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either equivalent value.

modelAnswer: The least count of an instrument is the smallest measurement that it can measure accurately.
The least count of a metre rule is 1 mm (0.1 cm).

items.followUp: Define rotatory motion and give one example.

rubric.why: Checks the defining feature of translatory motion.
rubric.description: States that all parts of the body move the same distance in the same direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

rubric.description: Gives a suitable example of translatory motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an example such as a car moving along a straight road.

modelAnswer: Translatory motion is motion in which all parts of a body move the same distance in the same direction.
Example: A car moving along a straight road.
